title: Who gets the book?
description: This compact IOI-style model receives two names and a subject-role marker. It predicts the other name as the indirect object. Find the heads that read the subject role and move the correct name to the output.
behavior: Given NAME_A, NAME_B, and a subject marker, predict the other name at QUERY.
task_goal: Identify the subject-finding and name-moving heads, show their attention targets, and causally verify both on held-out name pairs.
example_note: SUBJECT_A means the first name gave the book; SUBJECT_B means the second name did. Predict the other person.
learning_objectives: Follow role information through a circuit
Distinguish subject finding from name moving
Use head ablation to test a multi-head explanation
hints: Find which token encodes the subject role.
Inspect layer 0 head 0 at the final query position.
Inspect layer 2 head 1 to see which name position it routes to.
Ablate the subject-finding and name-moving heads separately.
starter_code:
def solve(model, tokenizer, dataset, tools):
    tokens = dataset[0]["tokens"]
    print("IOI accuracy:", tools.evaluate(dataset)["accuracy"])
    print("Subject read:", tools.attention(tokens, 0, 0)[-1])
    print("Name moved:", tools.attention(tokens, 2, 1)[-1])
    subject_head = tools.ablate_head(tokens, 0, 0)
    name_mover = tools.ablate_head(tokens, 2, 1)
    print("Causal effects:", subject_head, name_mover)
    return {"components": [{"type": "attention_head", "layer": 0, "head": 0}, {"type": "attention_head", "layer": 2, "head": 1}]}

explanation.canonical_solution: Layer 0 head 0 reads the subject-role marker. Layer 2 head 1 routes from the non-subject name position to the answer logits. Ablating either stage damages the IOI answer on balanced hidden name pairs.
explanation.caution: Attention to a name is only a routing observation; ablation and held-out name pairs provide causal and generalization evidence.

grading_contract.checks: Must identify exactly the subject head (layer 0, head 0) and name-moving head (layer 2, head 1).

grading_contract.type: list[{type: ablation, layer: int, head: int, measured values: float}]
grading_contract.checks: Must record both ablations with drop ≥ 0.25. Hidden baseline must equal 1.0 and mean hidden drop must be ≥ 0.25.

tool_reference.name: tools
tool_reference.description: A helper object passed into solve(...). Use it to measure behavior and inspect or intervene on this challenge model.

tool_reference.name: tools.evaluate(dataset)
tool_reference.description: Measures task performance across records. Returns accuracy, correct, and total.

tool_reference.name: tools.attention(tokens, layer, head)
tool_reference.description: Returns the attention matrix. Row i shows where the query at token position i reads; columns are key positions.

tool_reference.name: tools.ablate_head(tokens, layer, head)
tool_reference.type: dict: {type:str, layer:int, head:int, before:float, after:float, drop:float}
tool_reference.description: Temporarily zeros one head and measures task accuracy before and after. Records an ablation event; drop is before minus after.

tool_reference.name: tools.ablation_sweep(tokens)
tool_reference.description: Runs ablate_head on every head for one token sequence, sorted by largest accuracy drop. Pass tokens, e.g. dataset[0]["tokens"], not the whole dataset.

tool_reference.name: tools.activation(tokens, name)
tool_reference.description: Reads a named activation tensor, such as a residual stream or MLP activation.

tool_reference.name: tools.logit_lens(tokens, layer=None)
tool_reference.description: Projects a residual stream through the unembedding to see token scores at a layer.

tool_reference.name: tools.weight(name, layer=None, head=None)
tool_reference.description: Reads a model weight matrix, such as W_Q, W_K, W_V, or W_O.
